column1: # OPEN LOOPS -- a log of things that will one day CLOSE.
# Append-only. One row per loop EVENT, not one row per loop: `open`, `close`,
# `supersede`, `note`. The set of open loops is DERIVED by taking the latest
# verb for each id -- so there is no mutable `closed` cell to go stale, which is
# what the first draft of this file got wrong.
# WHY IT EXISTS: four errors of one shape. A forward-looking note was written,
# it fired, and nobody closed it:
#   * articles.md art. 11 warned the Wace receipt would reach Wend before she
#     had seen the letter. TRUE ON DAY 55, FIRED ON DAY 65, quoted as live on
#     DAY 77 -- eleven days late.
#   * npcs.md said of Ancel "Unanswered. He will not sit in the square forever."
#     ANSWERED ON DAY 34 and quoted as live on DAY 77 -- FORTY-THREE DAYS.
#   * CHECKLIST section 11 was headed "day 39" while play stood at day 77, and
#     warned in its own second paragraph that snapshots rot.
#   * "Rowe stays until his foot heals" long after he went south with Halm.
# A warning is the one kind of prose that never LOOKS stale. A stale total looks
# like a number and can be checked against a tool; a stale warning looks like a
# warning. So warnings become rows with a due date and a close-out.
# *** `close` REQUIRES `evidence`, and tools/loops.py refuses without it. ***
# A loop cannot be closed with a flag. Closing means CITING THE THING THAT
# CLOSED IT -- which is precisely the step that was skipped on art. 11. Evidence
# is a pointer: "65:2" (day:seq in interactions), "calendar.md:72", a TSV line.
# WHAT MAY NOT GO IN HERE. The test is: DOES IT HAVE A MOMENT AT WHICH IT STOPS
# BEING TRUE?
#   LOOP          "the wool party back ~83"  "Ancel returns in spring"
#   LOGGED FACT   "Cuddy is frail"  "Perrin refers upward"   -> npcs.md / interactions
#   FINDING       "gifts land badly, work lands"              -> articles.md
# If facts get in here the list grows for ever, the DM stops reading it, and it
# becomes the next CHECKLIST.md.
# Seeded 2026-09-11 by walking CHECKLIST section 11 and every warning box in
# articles.md. That walk WAS the first audit. See dlwork/tooling_plan.md phase 1.

Ancel asked OSK, in front of the party, who to speak to about next summer's wool -- the first outside buyer to ask in two years

ANSWERED COMPLETELY on day 34: introduced to Wend as factor (127), brokered to Marrow (114), four buyers named, a penny in the pound for three years. *** This is the 43-day loop. It is seeded first on purpose, as the worked example of what this file is for. ***
Master Wace's receipt for the account of movables -- Toller's day-42 condition turns on it, and Wend will have it before she has seen the letter

RECEIPT ARRIVED and recites the contents. Toller paid ~250 gp the same day; his condition DISCHARGED AND CLOSED. Over a thousand gold for the first time. *** The eleven-day loop. Second worked example. ***
The six holders' 229 gp of shares, in a strongbox, not the party's money
The art. 7 floor chalked on the board and read to every holder
Halm's standing want, asked once and never again: "one load's a load. What I'd want is a RUN." Wend is for it on one condition -- a load both ways
What a dwarf is owed. Cuddy has written to his own house; the dwarf waits above ground on trestles until an answer comes
The Michaelmas licence payment, 25 gp a year for three years from Michaelmas last
Toller wants SIX CORRESPONDENTS IN SIX TOWNS -- "two dealers in one town who know each other is one price"
18 gp owing to Lyde in three further quarterly instalments; next about day 152
28 gp owing from Holt in his own hand against the cask, as he draws it
Holt asked to be told if anyone ever learns whose brewhouse 'SD' was
Toller asked ONE thing: tell him FIRST if anything ever goes south instead of to him
Forty unnamed jars of chemicals for Trebb the dyer at Marchford -- Toller handed them off entirely: "forty of anything isn't curio, it's STOCK"
The wool-buying party home -- Nan grades, Tam writes, Hask holds the price, Halm carts, Rowe minds the beasts
Find Dill his trade or lose him. Hask's proposal is TEACHING, not labour: a year to make two dressers. Wend: don't find him a shovel
The Draycot chapel roof -- whose is it. Ottir: ask WHO MENDED IT LAST and who paid, and the man to ask is Cuddy. Perrin struck off. Do not ask the hall
*** A MAN HAS BEEN SENT ABOUT THE ANIMATED DEAD. *** No name, no rank, no date. Cuddy's house did not write to ask questions -- it wrote to say a man is coming
Wend needs ONE answer before she will cost the southern list: HOW MUCH, and WHOSE MONEY
Ask Bern what he wants off a Ludbury list -- the reed and the heddles, not the frame. Do not order over his head
Wend to order the narrow loom from Bern and send Lyde the joiner's name, and to hire her two
Osk back off his Marchford run. Three things: whether the party is entering his trade, the standing-run question, and he is the man Ancel asked about the wool
SOUTH with three carts after the 83rd -- Wend's list costed, Toller's correspondents, the jars, and "who buys narrow cloth in Marchford and at what"
Gyll's four-and-a-bit acres for flax. Ottir's condition: ask the eleven, one at a time, and NOBODY goes near Gyll first
The iron price -- price the NEW properly and SHOW THE ROAD IN THE PRICE. Do not reprice the old
Sarn onto Coll's standing roll at a clerk's wage. Wend and Coll are doing it; the party is not to be involved, and nobody tells Sarn it is because he was owed it
Wat's terms -- Coll's to settle, the party has stood back
ANCEL RETURNS IN SPRING WITH A PURSE, on a penny in the pound for three years -- and his four buyers include a FULLER WHO TAKES CLOTH, which is the answer-shaped thing to Wend's narrow-cloth question
Tristle is 539 xp from 2nd level -- which is what unfreezes the pit trap at (29,31), the only known way to level 2
The plain metal ring from the area 27 dais is still unidentified. Only lead is WRAYE, three days east of Ludbury, which has a library
Areas 10 and 11 are mis-mapped and the party must not be taken there
Level 2 is built and merged but entirely unexplored -- two exits from room 50 and something in the east passage
EXPEDITION 9 FOOD: eight people have ~4 days underground. 3 gp a person-week standard, 5 gp iron, purse with Wend
